title: Pruning Autonomous Driving VLAs: What to Preserve for Reasoning and Action
description: Reasoning vision-language-action (VLA) models for autonomous driving use chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning to guide action generation, but incur substantial memory and computational costs. We study structured pruning for these models, focusing on preserving both scene understanding and trajectory prediction. Our analysis of Taylor importance in Alpamayo-1.5-10B shows that reasoning and trajectory objectives assign different importance to the same vision-language model (VLM) structures. In the act...

title: Let Vision-Language Models Generate Images through Their Representations
description: Recent unified multimodal models aim to combine visual understanding and generation within a single model, yet effectively integrating the two capabilities remains challenging. Leveraging pretrained vision-language models offers a way to build on already learned multimodal knowledge, but making this knowledge effectively accessible to visual generation remains nontrivial. We find that a central challenge lies in the heterogeneous visual representations used for understanding and generation. To a...

title: TowerBridge: Bridging the Dual-Encoder Modality Gap via Weight-Space Programming
description: CLIP-style dual encoders map images and text through two separate towers into a shared embedding space, where the two modalities occupy distinct regions separated by a modality gap. Retrieval fails when wrong matches, or hard negatives, outrank the correct one, and the gap is the usual suspect. Yet removing it post hoc degrades retrieval on every CLIP checkpoint we test. We introduce a paired statistic that identifies directions where the two towers agree more on hard negatives than on matched p...

title: Language Models Steer on Injected Uncertainty Tokens, but Fail to Self-Monitor In Situ
description: Prompting language models to verbalize stepwise numerical confidence during generation is an increasingly popular approach for triggering backtracking and error correction in agentic reasoning. This strategy presupposes two capabilities: (1) in-situ monitoring fidelity (does confidence drop when an error occurs?) and (2) downstream steering control (does an uncertainty token causally steer the model to repair its error?). We evaluated four open-weights models (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, Mistral-7...

title: How Far Can Linear Go? BiPert, a Unified Framework for Single-Cell Perturbation Modelling
description: Understanding how genetic perturbations affect cellular behaviour is essential for studying gene function and regulatory mechanisms. Large-scale CRISPR screens measure these effects across thousands of genes, but cover relatively few cellular contexts. Predicting perturbation responses in unseen cell types and identifying perturbed genes from their transcriptional effects therefore remain challenging. Here, we show that both tasks can be addressed through a common linear decomposition of transcr...

title: Self-Supervised Dataset Distillation via Mutual Information Maximization
description: Dataset distillation (DD) aims to compress a large dataset into a small synthetic one that remains effective for training neural networks. Despite its success in supervised learning, DD remains underexplored in self-supervised learning (SSL), where distilled data must preserve the information needed to learn representations that remain consistent across augmentations. To bridge this gap, we introduce Mutual Information Prototype Alignment (MIPA), an efficient SSL dataset distillation approach th...

title: Agentic AI for Intent Management and Control in Autonomous Communication Networks
description: Artificial intelligence (AI)-driven automation will help future mobile networks translate high-level network intents into concrete network optimization or control actions. However, existing approaches often focus on intent management and orchestration, leaving the adaptation of underlying network optimization and control functions largely unaddressed. This article proposes a triadic agentic AI framework that co-designs intent management and intent fulfillment through three agents: an interpreter...

title: CTLink: A Text-Prompted Segmentation Model for Linking Radiology Report Findings to 3D Chest CT Scans
description: Radiology reports describe findings in text only, without visually marking them on the scan, so readers cannot directly see which abnormality each reported finding refers to. We introduce CTLink, a text-prompted 3D segmentation model that segments findings described in a chest CT report. CTLink was trained on 4123 noncontrast chest CT scans with 9547 segmented report findings, including ReXGroundingCTv2, a newly annotated dataset of 1134 scans and 1895 findings with every instance of each findin...

title: LeJEPA Features Are Not Isotropic, and Should Not Be
description: The SIGReg term in LeJEPA regularizes features to have an isotropic Gaussian distribution. Our first result is to show that this regularizer, in practice, cannot achieve its goal. We design a modified regularizer to enforce the objective better. This leads to slightly improved performance. For example, on ImageNet-100, our modified regularizer reaches the final accuracy of SIGReg in 1.3$\times$ fewer epochs. Our second result argues that self-supervised encoders should not have isotropic Gaussia...

title: Seeking in Space: Benchmarking Purposeful Active Exploration of Vision-Language Models for Spatial Reasoning
description: Humans explore unfamiliar spaces with purpose, deciding where to look until they have gathered the evidence a spatial question requires. However, can vision-language models (VLMs), which reason increasingly well over curated images and videos, also seek in space when the evidence is not handed to them? We present ActSpace-Bench, a benchmark of 994 questions across 234 exploration episodes in 72 real-scanned indoor scenes, where a model starts from a single view, navigates real captured frames, a...

title: Flood forecasting using a physics-guided conditional denoising diffusion probabilistic model
description: High-resolution flood forecasting with full two-dimensional shallow water equation (SWE) solvers remains computationally expensive, even on GPUs. We develop a conditional denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) that forecasts the evolution of 30 m water-depth fields over a four-day horizon for the Des Plaines River watershed, Illinois. The model is trained on SynxFlow SWE simulations of 113 historical storms observed across twelve Midwestern states (2003-2024), each under three antecedent...

title: huggingface/transformers Release v5.24.0
description: # Release v5.24.0 ## New Model additions ### Inkling 2 Mini Inkling 2 Mini is a multimodal model from Thinking Machines Lab that accepts text and image inputs and generates text outputs. It is a smaller sibling of Inkling 2 Small, added in v5.23.0. It has 24 decoder layers instead of 48, and compensates with a looping mechanism in which layers 6 to 17 run three times. A learned message-passing mechanism mixes the residuals of the previous pass into the attention and mixture-of-experts inputs of each loop layer. The decoder has a hidden size of 2304 and routes each token to 8 of 128 experts. The image encoder, tokenizer and processor are the same as Inkling 2 Small's. A research checkpoint ([TML-d24-varloop-research](https://huggingface.co/thinkingmachines/TML-d24-varloop-research)) has the same architecture but supports a variable number of loop passes. Fewer passes are faster, and more passes improve quality. Both checkpoints contain NVFP4 and MXFP8 quantized layers, which are dequantized at load time. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/inkling2_loop) | [Blog Post](https://thinkingmachines.ai/news/inkling-2-mini/) | [HF Blog Post](https://huggingface.co/blog/inkling2mini) * Add Inkling2 Mini (#51050) by @guarin ### Apertus 1.5 Apertus 1.5 is a multimodal model from the Swiss AI Initiative that accepts text, images and audio and generates text. It extends the Apertus language model with the EMU3.5 vision tokenizer for images and WavTokenizer for audio. The EMU3.5 tokenizer is an image-only VQGAN with the same encoder as Chameleon's, and it assigns codes by the largest inner product with the codebook. ## v2.14.4 (2026-11-19)

### What's Changed

#### Packaging

* Bump jiter to v0.19.0 by @Viicos in [#14247](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/pull/14247).
  This addresses memory issues introduced by the previous jiter release.

#### Changes

* Don't mark subclasses of `@deprecated` classes as deprecated in JSON Schema by @Viicos in [#14325](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/pull/14325)

#### Performance

* Cache UTC `TzInfo` instance by @Viicos in [#14256](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/pull/14256)
* Skip schema deduplication for alternatives with a single schema by @fredheir in [#14274](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/pull/14274)

#### Fixes

* Exclude `InitVar` fields from the serialization JSON schema by @Alvi-Rahman in [#14223](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/pull/14223)
* Fix more issues about GC tracking in `pydantic-core` by @Viicos in [#14253](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/pull/14253)
* Fix validation constraints leaking into the `Decimal` JSON Schema by @aidxhxr in [#14254](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/pull/14254)
* Fix model signature when a field alias is the name used for extra kwargs by @aidxhxr in [#14255](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/pull/14255)
* Fix display of `Callable` parameters in type representations by @aidxhxr in [#14261](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/pull/14261)
* Respect validation-time `strict=True` for `complex` by @Viicos in [#14293](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/pull/14293)
* Fill missing type alias arguments from type parameter defaults by @Viicos in [#14324](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/pull/14324)

title: agno-agi/agno v3.2.1
description:
# Changelog

## New Features:
- **Session Compactions**: `GET /sessions/{session_id}/compactions` lists a session's compactions on `SqliteDb` and `PostgresDb`, newest first, with how many messages each replaced and the token count before and after.
- **Company Files**: A Task's files and the shared notes can now be read over the API with `GET /company/tasks/{task_id}/files` and `GET /company/notes`, each with a `/{path}` route to read one file. See [cookbook](https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/blob/main/cookbook/05_agent_os/30_company/16_company_file_tree.py).

## Improvements:
- **LinearTools, DiscordTools and ModelsLabTools**: Now take a `timeout` (default 30 seconds, 120 for ModelsLab) that applies to every request.
- **ExaTools**: Now takes `include_text`, `exclude_text`, `user_location`, `moderation`, `highlights` and `subpages`.
- **MCPTools**: `connect()` now returns `True` when connected and `False` when not.
- **Qdrant**: `async_insert` now takes `batch_size`, like `insert`.
- **WebSearchTools and DuckDuckGoTools**: Search errors now come back as a JSON result.
- **Skills**: Skill instructions, references and script output in Chinese and other non-ASCII languages now reach the model as readable characters.
- **AntigravityTools and AntigravityAgent**: Now default to `antigravity-preview-09-2026`.
- **Slack**: `default_role` gives Slack members not in `users=` the permissions of a managed role. Each member is still recorded as themselves.

## Bug Fixes:
- **SQLTools**: A `db_engine` you pass in is now always used, even when connection fields are also given, and `run_sql_query` now returns the database error when reading the result rows fails.
- **OpenRouter, Perplexity and Requesty**: Responses now use the model's own output limit when `max_tokens` is not set, so long answers come back complete.
- **OpenRouterResponses**: Run and message metrics now include the `cost` that OpenRouter reports for each request.
- **Traces**: `GET /traces` now

title: huggingface/transformers Release v5.23.0
description: # Release v5.23.0 ## New Model additions ### Inkling2 Inkling 2 Small is a multimodal model from Thinking Machines Lab that accepts text and image inputs and generates text outputs, and it is intended for use in English and other languages and across multiple coding languages. Its language backbone has 48 mixture-of-experts decoder layers, each routing tokens to 8 of 384 experts, for 594B total and 17B active parameters. It keeps the Inkling decoder (learned relative attention, short causal convolutions, mixture-of-experts layers) and adds block attention residuals, gated attention with a learned sink, and dynamic key/value convolutions. Images are encoded by a Perception Encoder-based vision transformer and projected into the language model embeddings, one embedding per 40x40 pixel patch. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/inkling2) | [Blog Post](https://thinkingmachines.ai/news/inkling-2-small/) * Add inkling2 (#50682) by @guarin in [#50682](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/50682) ### JEV JEV is a decision head that scores single-token labels with a linear layer at the last token of the prompt, soft-capped like the logits of a language model head. `JevForDecision` is the model of the checkpoint and its head, and it reads the head files shipped next to the weights (`head.safetensors` and `judge_config.json` for JEV). The same head is also used by GEV and reads the 255 answer codes of pplx-decider and d3, and it can be run through the experimental `decision` pipeline or directly with `decide`. **Note:** JEV and the decision pipeline are currently experimental. Their APIs, configuration, and behavior may change as development continues. They should be used with caution in production environments. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface
